author: fab_10
content:
which is the right thing to do when receiving invalid bytes or encoded txs as input of FcU+attrs? 
1. return invalid payload params, or 2. just ignore the invalid entries and proceed with the valid ones?

author: raxhvl
content:
From [proposed spec update:](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12470/changes)

> 2. Decode `T`. If decoding fails or `T` specifies a different chain ID, continue to the next transaction.

author: fab_10
content: thanks, this section if for `newPayload` though, it seems natural to assume the same for FcU+attrs, but for extra clarity isn't it worth to repeat the same rules apply to FcU as well?

author: raxhvl
content:
The [payload building](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/blob/main/src/engine/bogota.md#payload-building) states same IL constraints apply.

In the engine API, `PayloadAttributesV5.inclusionListTransactions`  is defined as:

> Array of DATA - Array of transaction objects, each object is a byte list (DATA) representing TransactionType || TransactionPayload or LegacyTransaction as defined in EIP-2718.

It should just be `Array of DATA` as this interface is not responsible for ensuring the data decodes to a valid tx and does not throw an error because of  it  (same for `engine_newPayloadV6`)

author: jih2nn
content: Good point, it should be. Let me reflect this point in the EIP, thanks!

author: jih2nn
content: Good point, I think the design intention here is that an IL transaction of invalid format doesn't neutralize the entire IL process. We could use the EIP to deliver this clearly.
